metric.package_ecosystem_activity_mainte.score_rationale: Every sampled package across core domains (web framework, HTTP client, CLI parsing, database, crypto, and async networking core) shows issue/PR closures and releases within days to a few months of the snapshot date, and several (Vapor, swift-crypto, SwiftNIO) carry official SSWG or Apple maintenance backing that provides institutional continuity. The overall Swift Package Index itself is actively maintained (recently joined Apple, added maintenance-recency display to search results) and indexes a five-figure package catalog. This indicates strong, consistent maintenance activity, though the ecosystem is smaller in absolute package count than the largest general-purpose ecosystems and some community packages (e.g., Alamofire) explicitly note platform-support limitations that constrain otherwise-active maintenance.

metric.third_party_library_availability_.methodology_note: Predeclared sampling: domains were fixed before evidence collection. Selection rule: for each domain, prefer the package explicitly curated/listed on the official swift.org/packages page or a package that has 'Graduated' status in the Swift Server Workgroup (SSWG) incubation process; where no such official curation exists for a domain, select the highest GitHub-star Swift-language package surfaced by Swift Package Index / GitHub search for that domain's canonical keyword. Retrieval route: web search against swiftpackageindex.com, github.com, and swift.org pages. Snapshot time: 2026-09-22.
metric.third_party_library_availability_.score_rationale: Swift has mature, officially-endorsed (Apple/SSWG) or long-lived community libraries covering the classic backend/mobile domains: server-side web (Vapor), async networking core (SwiftNIO), HTTP client (Alamofire), database (GRDB), cryptography (swift-crypto), logging (swift-log), and CLI parsing (swift-argument-parser). Coverage is comparatively thin outside Apple-platform-oriented and server domains: Alamofire itself documents unsupported status on Linux/Windows/Android, and swift.org's own curated package categories are limited to a handful of areas (macros, server, networking, testing, logging, database) with no official category for data science/ML or general cross-platform desktop GUI. This produces solid-but-not-comprehensive domain coverage relative to ecosystems with broader footprints.
